answer: Like an orchard where each trellis holds only a few vines, admission grows through a scarce invitation quota: each established identity may invite at most two newcomers per epoch, and each invitee spends a full epoch on probation, unable to attest or vote. If an invitee is exposed as a duplicate, the inviter loses its own standing and all its invitees face a fresh audit, so one bad invite poisons the river downstream. An attacker must sacrifice a genuine identity for every two fakes. The limit: patient attackers with many seed identities can still grow slowly, and newcomers need an inviter.
